'''Vitaly Alekseevich Korotich''' ({{langx|ru|Виталий Алексеевич Коротич}}; {{langx|uk|Віталій Олексійович Коротич}}, ''Vitaliy Oleksiyovych Korotych''; 26 May 1936 – 29 September 2025) was a Soviet, Ukrainian and Russian writer, journalist, poet<ref name=ist>{{Cite web|title=IN MEMORIAM: Помер поет Віталій Коротич|date=2025-09-30|url=https://www.istpravda.com.ua/short/2025/09/30/165358/|access-date=2025-10-01}}</ref> and KGB agent.<ref>[http://www.newlookmedia.ru/IDNV/Redakcia/Stranic/Kolumnisty.html Издательский дом "Новый Взгляд". О музыке, кино, политике легко! КОЛУМНИСТЫ «НОВОГО ВЗГЛЯДА»]. Newlookmedia.ru. Retrieved on 2010-12-22.</ref><ref>[http://newlookmedia.ru/IDNV/Novyj_Vzglad/Stranic/Novyj_vzglad_1993.html#9 Газета «Новый Взгляд»]. Newlookmedia.ru. Retrieved on 2010-12-22.</ref><ref>[http://newlookmedia.ru/IDNV/Novyj_Vzglad/Stranic/Novyj_vzglad_1994.html#19 Газета «Новый Взгляд»]. Newlookmedia.ru. Retrieved on 2010-12-22.</ref>

== Life and career ==
Korotich was born on 26 May 1936 in [[Kyiv]].<ref name=ist/> He graduated from the Kyiv Medical University in 1959 and worked as a doctor between 1959 and 1966. Later, he became a full-time writer, and served as an officer of the [[Union of Soviet Writers]].<ref name=ljw1976>Marshall Fine, [https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=4LYrAAAAIBAJ&sjid=A-YFAAAAIBAJ&pg=6746,4263879&dq=korotich&hl=en Poet provides a view of Soviet Writers], Lawrence Journal-World, Sep 28, 1976</ref>

In the late 1970s, Korotich became the editor of ''[[Vsesvit]]'', a Ukrainian literary magazine in Kyiv specializing in publishing literary works translated from foreign languages.<ref>{{citation
|first=Joseph |last=Gibbs
|publisher=Texas A&M University Press |year=1999
|isbn=0-89096-892-6
|title=Gorbachev's glasnost: the Soviet media in the first phase of perestroika
|series=Volume 9 of Eastern European studies
|url= https://books.google.com/books?id=Q3hvBm1s-FQC&pg=PA110
|page=110
}}</ref> His magazine was described at the time as one "that probably prints more of the latest American fiction than any magazine in Moscow."<ref>Anthony Austin, [https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=Qe0cAAAAIBAJ&sjid=rGcEAAAAIBAJ&pg=6915,1002874&dq=korotich&hl=en Americans sense new vitality in Soviet writers], Sarasota Herald-Tribune – Sep 16, 1979</ref>

In 1976, Korotich spent three weeks as a writer-in-residence at the [[University of Kansas]] in [[Lawrence, Kansas]].<ref name=ljw1976/> In 1984, still the editor-in-chief of ''Vsesvit'', he was in New York as a member of the [[Ukrainian SSR]]'s delegation at the [[United Nations General Assembly]].<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=C-L8AAAAMAAJ&q=vsesvit+korotich List of delegations – United Nations. General Assembly]</ref>
In 1985, he visited Canada as well, participating in a campaign for world peace and for nuclear disarmament.<ref>[https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=VGA_AAAAIBAJ&sjid=blMMAAAAIBAJ&pg=4833,2126870&dq=korotich&hl=en Disparate trio joins to combat nuclear weapons], The Saturday Windsor Star – Jun 8, 1985</ref>

In the late 1980s and early 1990s Korotich was editor-in-chief of ''[[Ogonyok]]'' magazine in Moscow, which made, some say, a substantial contribution to the promotion of media freedom in the former [[USSR]]. The ''Ogonyok'' magazine, at the time when Korotich was at its head, was regarded as a "megaphone" for the [[perestroika]] and [[glasnost]] policies of the last USSR President [[Mikhail Gorbachev]].

In 1992 Korotich went to the United States and was a visiting professor of journalism at [[Boston University]], also lecturing at [[Boston College]] on 19 October.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ukrainian journalist to speak |url=https://newspapers.bc.edu/?a=d&d=bcchronicle19921015-01.2.9&e=-------en-20--1--txt-txIN------- |date=15 October 1992 |access-date=19 February 2022 |work=Boston College Chronicle |volume=1 |issue=4 |publisher=Boston College}}</ref>

According to Korotich, he did not have a Ukrainian passport. He believed that Crimea should be under Russian protectorate and independent from Ukraine.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Jongeneel |first1=Judith |title=The weekly Ogonyok in Soviet and American public discourse. The image of the Soviet liberalisations in East and West (1986—1991) |access-date=1 October 2025 | url=https://scripties.uba.uva.nl/document/654689 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200131061913/https://scripties.uba.uva.nl/document/654689 |archive-date= 31 January 2020 |page=11}}</ref> He later approved of the [[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russian invasion]] of his native Ukraine.<ref>{{cite news |title=Умер Виталий Коротич — украинский поэт и редактор перестроечного «Огонька» |url=https://www.bbc.com/russian/articles/c4nn2qp27z0o |access-date=1 October 2025 |work=BBC News Russian |date=30 September 2025 |language=ru}}</ref> In 2024, he stated that "a war is being waged against Russia", while "Ukraine is just an expandable."<ref>{{cite news |title=Коротич: Конфликт на Украине стал для США пьянкой, на которой не трезвеют |url=https://www.kp.ru/daily/27550/4875170/ |access-date=1 October 2025 |work=Komsomolskaya Pravda |date=1 January 2024 |language=ru}}</ref> He also called [[Volodymyr Zelenskyi]] "one of the most obedient American satellites" and said that Americans "forbid him from negotiating peace" and "could oust Zelensky" if he tried to negotiate with Russians again.<ref>{{cite news |title=Виталий Коротич: Американцы могли бы изгнать Зеленского с Украины |url=https://www.kp.ru/daily/27631.5/4982171/ |access-date=1 October 2025 |work=Komsomolskaya Pravda |date=8 September 2024 |language=ru}}</ref> Korotich died on 29 September 2025.<ref>[https://interfax.com.ua/news/general/1108625.html Виталий Коротич умер в Москве] {{in lang|ru}}</ref>

== Cooperation with KGB ==
In 1963, he was recruited by the [[KGB]] and was referred to as Agent Yanvarsky. His three-month stay in Canada in 1965 was believed to "contribute to the process of further disintegration of Ukrainian nationalist organisations abroad." Korotich was also informing the KGB against Ukrainian dissident poet [[Ivan Drach]] and the head of the [[Association of United Ukrainian Canadians]], Petro Kravchuk.<ref>{{cite news |title=Із поетів — у сексоти |url=https://ukrainainc.net/2024/12/19/20726/ |access-date=1 October 2025 |work=Ukrainian Worldwide Information Network |date=19 December 2024 |language=uk}}</ref>

==Literary activities==
Korotych was an author of several works of prose and poetry<ref name=ist/> in [[Ukrainian language]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Віталій Коротич (1936)|url=https://maysterni.com/user.php?id=1962&t=1&sf=1|access-date=2025-10-01}}</ref>
